transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-13 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Liu (Redwood SE), Ava Torres (Redwood Security PM), Priya Raman (Montara CISO), Ethan Cole (Montara Cloud Ops), Lina Ortiz (Montara SecEng), Samir Patel (Montara Compliance)

Summary: short readout of our SOC 2/ISO posture and how Montara's controls map to Redwood's trust center. Focus on logs, RBAC, SSO, and KMS.

[00:00] Jenna Park: all right everyone, thanks for joining. this is Jenna from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. quick intros?
[00:08] Priya Raman: hi, this is Priya, CISO at Montara. thanks. we have Ethan, Lina and Samir with me.
[00:15] Ethan Cole: hey all.
[00:17] Marcus Liu: Marcus here, I'm the SE, i'll own the KMS and infra bits for today.
[00:23] Ava Torres: and i'm ava, security program manager — i'll help with controls mapping and evidence.
[00:28] Jenna Park: great. quick agenda: redwood artifacts we can share, trust center access, RBAC/SSO flow, audit logs/forensics, KMS options. then q&a and next steps. sound good?
[00:38] Priya Raman: yep. high level, Montara needs to know how you surface evidence to our auditors and whether we can keep keys in our KMS.
[00:46] Jenna Park: absolutely. Marcus do you want to start with report availability?
[00:50] Marcus Liu: sure. so we have a SOC 2 Type II report for our hosted platform, redacted copies are what we typically share — we remove customer-specific data but include control narratives and test results. for ISO27001 we maintain a controls matrix aligned with annex A and can export scope sections.
[01:08] Lina Ortiz: when you say redacted, does that include redaction of customer IDs and account names? we've had auditors ask for the names to be present sometimes.
[01:16] Ava Torres: good question — redaction is typically customer-identifying fields and customer datasets. control assertions and test counts remain. if your auditor requires specific evidence that references Montara, we can discuss a bilateral NDA to share less-redacted versions.
[01:29] Samir Patel: okay, sounds reasonable. what's the turnaround for the redacted SOC2?
[01:32] Jenna Park: we can send the redacted SOC 2 by Friday (07/16).
[01:36] Ethan Cole: on trust center — how do we get to the runbooks and configuration snapshots? do you host a portal?
[01:42] Marcus Liu: yes, trust center is our portal for docs and evidence links. we can grant read-only access to named Montara users, and we support an evidence export bundle (zipped) for auditors. retention for artifacts is 24 months by default, extendable.
[01:57] Priya Raman: what about audit logs? we use a centralized SIEM and need raw logs for forensic timelines, not only aggregated metrics. can you stream logs to our S3 or to a collector?
[02:08] Marcus Liu: we support S3 export and also direct syslog / HTTPS push to collector endpoints. there are rate limits and batching behaviour to consider — we can provide a logs playbook.
[02:17] Lina Ortiz: is there guaranteed retention? our compliance needs 7 years for some data types — that seems long.
[02:23] Ava Torres: Redwood's default log retention in hosted tier is 18 months, you can buy extended retention or set up an external export to your S3 bucket for long-term archival. the export can be daily or near-real-time; there is also a compliance export with integrity hashes.
[02:36] Priya Raman: integrity hashes? can you expand?
[02:38] Marcus Liu: sure — when we export logs for compliance customers we optionally include a SHA-256 manifest so your auditor can verify no tampering. it's part of the evidence bundle.
[02:48] Ethan Cole: nice. on RBAC and SSO — we use Okta and have pretty granular groups. we don't want to replicate roles manually. how does Redwood map groups to roles?
[02:58] Jenna Park: we integrate with SAML/Okta and support SCIM for provisioning. roles are configurable in the console and you can map Okta groups to Redwood roles. Marcus, do you have the mapping example?
[03:08] Marcus Liu: yes — typical mapping: Okta group "redwood-admins" -> role admin (full access), "redwood-ops" -> role operator (deploy, view logs), "redwood-readonly" -> auditor. We can accept SAML assertions with groups, and also support SCIM to keep membership in sync.
[03:24] Lina Ortiz: any gotchas for nested groups?
[03:27] Marcus Liu: nested groups in Okta can be flattening — SCIM is cleaner. we sometimes see delays in membership sync when relying purely on assertions, so SCIM provisioning + periodic sync is recommended for enterprise setups.
[03:38] Priya Raman: okay. KMS — we want BYOK and to ensure Redwood cannot decrypt our customer content. what's your posture?
[03:46] Ava Torres: we support three main modes: Redwood-managed keys (simpler), customer-managed keys in cloud KMS with delegated access (BYOK), and an HSM-backed flow for private deployments where keys never leave your KMS. for hosted we can integrate with AWS KMS or GCP KMS; you rotate keys on your schedule and we use short-lived service keys for encryption operations.
[04:03] Samir Patel: so if we bring our key, can Redwood access plaintext?
[04:07] Marcus Liu: operationally Redwood will not retain your plaintext keys. with BYOK, the data encryption keys are wrapped by your KMS and we only hold wrapped keys. in the HSM-private option, there is an additional gate where decryption can only occur in customer-controlled environment. caveat: some platform features (search indexing, embeddings caching) need consideration — we can design around encrypted-at-rest, but some runtime decrypt is necessary in the serving path.
[04:33] Ethan Cole: that runtime decrypt is the issue; we need to know where it happens and who can access memory of the hosts.
[04:39] Marcus Liu: yes, that's valid. we can share our memory protection docs and kernel isolation notes. for dedicated or private deployments you can keep the serving tier inside your VPC and we can set up network policies to limit access.
[04:51] Priya Raman: for ISO scope: does Redwood's ISO27001 scope include the hosted inference path? we need scope evidence for the model serving fleet.
[04:59] Ava Torres: the ISO scope covers the hosted inference control set; we can show scoping diagrams. we also maintain control statements mapped to annex A clauses.
[05:06] Lina Ortiz: auditors sometimes ask for configuration drift evidence — do you keep historical IaC snapshots?
[05:11] Marcus Liu: yes, we keep infrastructure configuration snapshots per deployment and can export diffs for a given timeframe. in hosted tier those are and we retain them for 12 months by default.
[05:20] Priya Raman: how about incident response — if there's a suspected data exfiltration, what's the runbook and SLAs?
[05:26] Ava Torres: we have an incident response runbook with timelines: initial acknowledgement 1 hour, preliminary incident report 24 hours, full incident package within 7 days. we also have escalation contacts and we will share redacted post-mortems; for enterprise customers we can align on custom SLAs.
[05:42] Samir Patel: retention policies for logs — will exported logs include user-level metadata and request IDs?
[05:48] Marcus Liu: yes, exports include request IDs, user token hashes (not raw tokens), timestamps, and service traces. PII is redacted by default unless you're doing a dedicated/private deployment where we can configure additional fields.
[05:59] Ethan Cole: we need S3 export with encryption using our KMS keys and an integrity manifest. is that supported?
[06:04] Marcus Liu: yes — S3 export with SSE-KMS using your key is supported. we can also sign manifests and place them in the bucket.
[06:12] Priya Raman: what about on-prem or VPC deployments — if we host on-prem can we get full access to logs, metrics, and the code bundle?
[06:21] Ava Torres: for private deployments we provide an on-prem package and can enable full log access and local KMS integration. code-sharing is negotiable; typically we provide runtime artifacts and configuration, not full source.
[06:34] Lina Ortiz: can you provide a short example of the RBAC export we can expect?
[06:38] Marcus Liu: sure — it's a CSV with columns: role_id, role_name, permissions_list, created_at, last_modified. We'll attach a sample in the follow-up email.
[06:49] Jenna Park: i'm going to pull up a quick slide on the trust center layout — so trust center has three levels: public docs, customer-specific evidence, and auditor bundles. named users get read-only to the customer-specific bucket. auditor bundles are time-limited links.
[07:05] Priya Raman: who owns access revocation when someone leaves Montara? can we control that centrally?
[07:11] Marcus Liu: yes, if you use SCIM provisioning we will honor deprovision events. otherwise, you can revoke sessions and user accounts from the console.
[07:19] Ethan Cole: are there any known gaps you have for SOC2 that we should be prepared to ask auditors about?
[07:24] Ava Torres: we are typically asked to show controls for vendor management and third-party dependencies; we have vendor attestations but auditors sometimes request deeper subcontractor certificates — we can provide a list and our third-party risk assessment.
[07:36] Priya Raman: acceptable. on the evidence export, would you include control test sample IDs?
[07:41] Marcus Liu: yes, the SOC report includes test sample descriptions. the evidence bundle will reference those and we can link to test artifacts where allowed.
[07:50] Samir Patel: about data residency — Montara's production data must stay in eu-west-1 and ap-south-1 for backups. do you support region pinning?
[07:58] Jenna Park: we do region pinning for dedicated and private deployments; for hosted customers we can provision regionally — we need to review your account tenancy to confirm. Marcus, can you add regional availability notes?
[08:08] Marcus Liu: yes, i will include a regional deployment matrix outlining where artifacts and backups live for hosted vs dedicated.
[08:16] Lina Ortiz: one more on loglineage — auditors ask to show chain of custody of logs. do you provide cryptographic verification?
[08:24] Ava Torres: yes, that's the manifest i mentioned — SHA-256 hashes plus timestamped manifests signed by our system. we can also timestamp to a third-party anchor if needed.
[08:36] Ethan Cole: okay good. any constraints on throughput when streaming logs? we don't want to impact inference latency.
[08:43] Marcus Liu: streams are buffered and we use async exporters. there's a small CPU/bandwidth footprint; for very high volumes we recommend a dedicated logging endpoint or pushing to your collector to keep serving lanes clear. we can simulate expected throughput in a poc.
[08:59] Priya Raman: about encryption in flight — TLS requirements? we require mutual TLS for internal services. does Redwood support mTLS?
[09:07] Marcus Liu: we support TLS1.2 and TLS1.3; mutual TLS is supported for private endpoints and for certain S3 ingest endpoints upon request.
[09:15] Samir Patel: are audit logs immutable once exported?
[09:18] Ava Torres: immutability at rest depends on how you store them. our export can write to an S3 bucket with object lock enabled if you want WORM retention, or we can publish to a write-once archive.
[09:30] Jenna Park: wrapping up the main points — we'll share the redacted SOC2 and ISO control mapping, provide RBAC sample CSV, regional matrix, and KMS integration notes. any outstanding questions?
[09:42] Priya Raman: I'd like to see the incident response SLAs in writing and a sample auditor bundle.
[09:49] Ava Torres: we'll include those in the follow-up.
[09:52] Ethan Cole: and the Terraform snippets for KMS?
[09:55] Marcus Liu: yes i'll include.
[09:57] Lina Ortiz: can we get a short tech deep-dive next week specifically on KMS flow and where runtime decryption happens?
[10:03] Jenna Park: sure— Marcus is available next week wednesday or thursday. i'll send a Doodle.
[10:10] Priya Raman: great. thanks everyone.
[10:12] Jenna Park: thanks all— we'll send the follow-ups and wrap.
notes: Transcript contains some ASR artifacts; company and product names occasionally mis-transcribed (e.g., 'Redwood' sometimes 'Red wood' in the ASR). Attendees agreed to a KMS deep-dive and evidence handoff timeline.
